checks.name: public-authority-interface-does-not-expose-solver-contract
checks.detail: Consumers can request an authoritative judgment but cannot retrieve/re-run the authority decision contract.

checks.name: decision-contract-is-private-to-authority-implementation
checks.detail: The existing semantic decision algebra contract remains implementation-owned and is not exported as a second consumer API.

checks.name: authority-interface-is-single-resolution-capability
checks.detail: The public authority capability is limited to resolving a typed request into a closed judgment.

checks.name: runtime-executor-interface-declares-upstream-ownership
checks.detail: The runtime boundary declares upstream authority ownership in its contract.

checks.name: executor-does-not-reason-or-read-contract-internals
checks.detail: Executor only delegates through the authority interface and contains no semantic solver dependency.

checks.name: executor-emits-authority-ownership-marker
checks.detail: Runtime executor instance conforms to the ownership marker promised by its interface.

checks.name: scanner-adapter-only-constructs-syntax-evidence
checks.detail: Scanner adapter maps AST structure into evidence and cannot own semantic rule execution.

checks.name: scanner-analyzer-consumes-executor-contract
checks.detail: Analyzer consumes the executor contract and no longer selects controller-variable semantic rules.

checks.name: composition-root-is-only-concrete-binding
checks.detail: Concrete authority-to-executor binding is isolated in the wiring composition root.

checks.name: judgment-remains-closed-and-evidence-bearing
checks.detail: The interface preserves the selected rule/evidence in resolved judgments and has an explicit closed contract-violation outcome.
